RagShortTexts: Order brethren differ in status from employees and attendants.
Vows do not remove food, equipment and care requirements.

Variants.Content: An Order house contains knight brethren, other brethren, employees and lay attendants with different duties. Vows bind professed members; hired and temporary followers have other arrangements. Kitchens, stables and workshops sustain armed service.
A spear-bearing attendant needs defined stable, equipment or fighting duties and a food provider. Proximity to a knight does not confer the same status.
Householders distinguish professed duties from paid work in discipline and reward. Unpaid labor or depleted stables harms effective strength despite martial appearances.
Cooks and repairers sustain the house without necessarily sharing its vows. Their work needs food and payment; families cannot live on promised spiritual merit.
